b6_reason: With mu = sqrt(3) and i = 60 deg, the refraction angle is 30 deg, and the reflected ray leaves at 60 deg on the other side of the normal, so the refracted and reflected rays are 180 - 60 - 30 = 90 deg apart.
b6_working: sin 60 / sin r = sqrt(3) => sin r = (sqrt(3)/2)/sqrt(3) = 1/2 => r = 30 deg; reflected ray at 60 deg from normal; angle between them = 180 - (60 + 30) = 90 deg
b6_note: Stem says 'refractive index 3' - the square-root sign was lost in extraction. Taken literally (mu = 3) r = 16.8 deg and the angle is about 103 deg, which matches no option; mu = sqrt(3) gives exactly option 3, so the radical is the likely original.
